namespace SM

noncomputable section
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
variable {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {P : LabelledTuple n} {j : ZMod n} {q : Plane} {ε : ℝ}

/-- Set exhaustion supplies a permutation; ordering is proved separately below. -/
theorem soft_gaussList_inherited_perm (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hP : Generic P)
    (hp : SoftCrossingPersistence P j q ε) (hQ : Generic (softInsertion P j q ε))
    (hclass : SoftCrossingClassificationAt P j q ε) :
    ((gaussList hn hP).map (softInheritedVisit hp)).Perm
      ((gaussList (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ).filter
        (fun w => decide (w.1.val ≠ {softOldIndex j (j - 1), softNewIndex j}))) := by
  apply (List.perm_ext_iff_of_nodup
    (List.Nodup.map (softInheritedVisit_injective hp) (gaussList_nodup hn hP))
    ((gaussList_nodup (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ).filter _)).mpr
  intro w
  constructor
  · rintro hw
    obtain ⟨v, _, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hw
    exact List.mem_filter.mpr ⟨mem_gaussList _ hQ _,
      decide_eq_true (softInheritedCrossing_ne_newborn hn hp v.1)⟩
  · intro hw
    have hne : w.1.val ≠ {softOldIndex j (j - 1), softNewIndex j} := by
      simpa only [decide_eq_true_eq] using (List.mem_filter.mp hw).2
    obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := (softInheritedVisit_range_iff hn hp hclass w).mpr hne
    exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨v, mem_gaussList hn hP v, rfl⟩

/-- Literal equality of the inherited sorted visit lists, including the
numerical cut and an empty parent list. It uses the actual geometric order. -/
theorem soft_gaussList_inherited (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hP : Generic P)
    (hp : SoftCrossingPersistence P j q ε) (hQ : Generic (softInsertion P j q ε))
    (hclass : SoftCrossingClassificationAt P j q ε)
    (ho : SoftInheritedOrderAt P j q ε) :
    (gaussList hn hP).map (softInheritedVisit hp) =
      (gaussList (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ).filter
        (fun w => decide (w.1.val ≠ {softOldIndex j (j - 1), softNewIndex j})) := by
  apply List.Perm.eq_of_pairwise
    (fun x y _ _ hxy hyx => visitKey_injective (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ
      (le_antisymm hxy hyx))
    _ ((gaussList_sorted (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ).filter _)
    (soft_gaussList_inherited_perm hn hP hp hQ hclass)
  apply List.pairwise_map.mpr
  apply (gaussList_sorted hn hP).imp
  intro v w h
  exact (softInheritedVisit_key_le_iff hn hP.1 hp hQ.1 ho v w).mpr h

/-- In all non-loop sectors every actual child visit is inherited. -/
theorem soft_gaussList_nonloop (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hP : Generic P)
    (hp : SoftCrossingPersistence P j q ε) (hQ : Generic (softInsertion P j q ε))
    (hclass : SoftCrossingClassificationAt P j q ε)
    (ho : SoftInheritedOrderAt P j q ε)
    (hnot : ¬ (softAttachmentMinus P j q = turn P j ∧ softAttachmentPlus P j q = turn P j)) :
    (gaussList hn hP).map (softInheritedVisit hp) =
      gaussList (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ := by
  rw [soft_gaussList_inherited hn hP hp hQ hclass ho]
  apply List.filter_eq_self.mpr
  intro w _
  obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := softInheritedVisit_surjective_nonloop hp hclass hnot w
  exact decide_eq_true (softInheritedCrossing_ne_newborn hn hp v.1)

/-- This equality is in the genuine rotation quotient of actual visits. -/
theorem soft_gaussCycle_nonloop (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hP : Generic P)
    (hp : SoftCrossingPersistence P j q ε) (hQ : Generic (softInsertion P j q ε))
    (hclass : SoftCrossingClassificationAt P j q ε)
    (ho : SoftInheritedOrderAt P j q ε)
    (hnot : ¬ (softAttachmentMinus P j q = turn P j ∧ softAttachmentPlus P j q = turn P j)) :
    (gaussCycle hn hP).map (softInheritedVisit hp) =
      gaussCycle (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ := by
  exact congrArg (fun l : List (Visit (softInsertion P j q ε)) =>
    (l : Cycle (Visit (softInsertion P j q ε))))
    (soft_gaussList_nonloop hn hP hp hQ hclass ho hnot)

/-- Crossing pairing is retained when passing from visits to the Gauss word. -/
theorem soft_gaussWord_nonloop (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hP : Generic P)
    (hp : SoftCrossingPersistence P j q ε) (hQ : Generic (softInsertion P j q ε))
    (hclass : SoftCrossingClassificationAt P j q ε)
    (ho : SoftInheritedOrderAt P j q ε)
    (hnot : ¬ (softAttachmentMinus P j q = turn P j ∧ softAttachmentPlus P j q = turn P j)) :
    (gaussWord hn hP).map (softInheritedCrossing hp) =
      gaussWord (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ := by
  have hl := congrArg (List.map Sigma.fst)
    (soft_gaussList_nonloop hn hP hp hQ hclass ho hnot)
  have he : ((gaussList hn hP).map Sigma.fst).map (softInheritedCrossing hp) =
      (gaussList (by omega : 3 ≤ n + 1) hQ).map Sigma.fst := by
    simpa only [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, softInheritedVisit_crossing] using hl
  exact congrArg (fun l : List (Crossing (softInsertion P j q ε)) =>
    (l : Cycle (Crossing (softInsertion P j q ε)))) he

end
end SM
evidence.root_log_limit: The successful root log prints the recorded axiom traces, not the full elaborated types of this group. Exact full statement texts, section context and proofs are bound by the body/prototype bytes. No reviewer elaboration or global canonical audit was run.

findings: The filtered child list is the actual canonical gaussList, filtered by inequality of each visit crossing support with the precise incoming/return newborn support. This is the previously proved inherited range predicate in every sector, not a freely supplied set of visits.

The permutation theorem first proves both lists have no duplicates: mapped parent visits use actual visit-map injectivity, and the child filter preserves canonical no-duplicates. It then proves membership equivalence. Forward membership uses the noninheritance of the newborn support; reverse membership uses the exact inherited visit range and the fact that the parent gaussList contains every actual parent visit.

The literal equality theorem does more than permutation. The mapped parent list is pairwise nondecreasing in the actual child visitKey by the canonical parent sortedness and the proved inherited key-order equivalence. The filtered child list remains sorted by the same relation. Antisymmetry follows from antisymmetry of real key values and child Generic visitKey injectivity. List.Perm.eq_of_pairwise therefore yields literal equality.

The numerical traversal cut is retained by the physical parent-edge value monotonicity used in key preservation. This includes j=0 and insertion after the source final physical vertex, where the return edge inherits residue zero. The sorted equality is not inferred from a mere cyclic relabelling or from a permutation.

In every non-loop sector, surjectivity of the actual inherited visit map shows that every child visit passes the filter. List.filter_eq_self removes the filter and gives literal equality with the complete child gaussList. The explicit non-loop hypothesis is the complement of the source loop conjunction; all other geometric premises are supplied on a positive interval by soft_small_visit_order_data under parent Generic and source admissibility.

The visit Cycle theorem takes this actual list equality through the canonical coercion to Cycle. The bound Mathlib definition is the quotient of lists by List.IsRotated, and Cycle.map lifts List.map. Thus the theorem is an identity in the genuine rotation quotient, not multiset equality or an arbitrary word construction.

The crossing-labelled word theorem maps Sigma.fst over the list equality. The exact inherited-visit crossing projection identifies that map with the inherited crossing map, and then the rotation quotient yields the actual canonical gaussWord identity. Crossing pairing is retained, with no freely chosen renaming beyond the proved support-image correspondence.

Every argument works for empty parent crossing and visit sets: no head, positive list length or selected crossing is used. Canonical sorting, filtering, mapping and the Cycle quotient all include empty lists. The filtered equality also applies in the loop sector, although no loop Cycle-filter or adjacency theorem is packaged by this group.

The first failure affected only two conversions from the proved support inequality to Boolean filter truth. Replacing those two proof fragments with decide_eq_true produces the frozen body exactly; substituting it produces the tested prototype. All five statement texts and their mathematical premises are unchanged. The first log retains its type mismatches and propagated sorryAx traces; the second root50181 log has all five standard foundational traces.
limits: This group proves sorted inherited-list equality in every sector and the full actual no-loop Cycle/Gauss-word map identities. It does not define a Cycle filter, prove the loop deletion identity directly in Cycle, construct the actual newborn visits, establish their oriented adjacency, or assemble all four source clauses with one radius.
